_note: The service-help-agent entry's requires.licenses and orderedSkills were validated by the feasibility spike (.context/test-drive-spike, 2026-08-24): the build runs end-to-end (author → local compile → deploy Apex → validate → deploy AiAuthoringBundle) and the agent's actions were verified against real org data. The conversational 'try it out' is interactive-only (sf agent preview is a TTY UI with no scriptable/headless mode), so it is a user-driven handoff step, never engine-verified. Channel wiring (website widget) and email-to-case are manual Setup steps, not skills — narrated as checkpoints at runtime.

testDrives.title: Service help agent (website chat widget)
testDrives.description: Build an Agentforce service agent that answers common customer questions, manages support cases, and hands off to a human — delivered as a chat widget on your website.

owner.contact: #service-cloud-agentforce (placeholder — confirm the owning team's durable channel)

testDrives.handoff: Try it immediately with the interactive preview. The agent is deployed as a draft (not published or activated), so you preview it straight from its local authoring bundle — run this one line: `cd "<projectDir>" && sf agent preview --target-org <targetOrg> --authoring-bundle <agentApiName> --use-live-actions`. The `cd` matters: `--authoring-bundle` reads the Agent Script bundle from inside the DX project, so the command must run from the project root — not `--api-name`, which only resolves for a published + activated agent and would fail here with `SingleRecordQuery_NoRecords`. (`sf agent preview` is an interactive terminal session; run it yourself.) Then ask a common question, ask it to open a support case, and ask to talk to a human — you'll see all three behaviors live. To put it in front of real customers, finish the narrated Setup step that wires the agent to a Messaging for Web / Embedded Service channel on your website.
